title: Implement the workspace invitation accept/redeem endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An invited user can redeem a valid scoped invite token to gain the granted workspace membership; redemption is single-use, expiry- and revocation-aware, tenant/workspace-scoped, and atomic (the WorkspaceMember is created and the invitation marked Accepted in one transaction); the authenticated caller who presents a valid token becomes the member (bearer grant); an invalid, expired, revoked or already-redeemed token grants nothing (fail-closed).
required_tests: Integration: a pending token redeems to exactly one WorkspaceMember carrying the invited role for the authenticated caller's subject; a second redemption of the same token is rejected (single-use); an expired or revoked token is rejected; a token presented for the wrong workspace/tenant is hidden-404; the redeemed member can then act per their role (e.g. create a scene) end-to-end over HTTP.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (workspace membership is currently UNREACHABLE via the public API - surfaced by hands-on testing 2026-06-15: a workspace creator is not auto-membered and the only way to gain membership is a direct DB seed). The domain is already built and unit-tested: WorkspaceInvitation.Redeem()/MatchesToken()/IsRedeemable() (WorkspaceInvitation.cs ~315-358), but CORE-WS-004 shipped only the invite half with NO acceptance route (WorkspaceEndpoints.cs ~40, IWorkspaceInvitationRepository.cs ~46). DECIDED MODEL (2026-06-15): the scoped token is a BEARER grant (T6) - whoever presents a valid token becomes the member; the invited email is DATA, never an identity/auth check. Add the redeem route taking the plaintext token in the request BODY, never in the URL path (tokens in URLs leak to logs, T7) - e.g. POST /api/v1/invitations/accept (token in body, resolved by its globally-unique token hash) or POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations/accept. Verify IsRedeemable, then Redeem() + create the WorkspaceMember for the AUTHENTICATED CALLER's OIDC subject with the invitation's role, and append an audit record - all in one CORE-CONC-002 transaction. Fail-closed; a bad/expired/revoked/foreign token is an indistinguishable rejection (T6). Add the route to csv/api_routes.csv and docs/08; reuse WorkspaceInvitationRepository + WorkspaceMemberRepository. Pairs with CORE-WS-007/008.

title: Implement the workspace invitation revoke endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An Owner/Admin can revoke a pending workspace invitation so its token can never be redeemed; revoking an already-accepted or already-revoked invitation is rejected; revocation is tenant/workspace-scoped and audited.
required_tests: Integration: a revoked invitation no longer redeems (with CORE-WS-006); only Owner/Admin may revoke (403 otherwise); revoking an accepted invitation is rejected; a foreign-tenant or unknown invitation is hidden-404.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (an invite cannot be taken back today - the T6 revocation control is unreachable). WorkspaceInvitation.Revoke() (WorkspaceInvitation.cs ~363-380) exists with no route. Add DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations/{invitationId} (or a .../revoke action). Owner/Admin only, mirroring the member-invite authorization (WorkspaceEndpoints.cs ~638-645). Reuse WorkspaceInvitationRepository; append an audit record. Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08. Depends on the invitation model; pairs with CORE-WS-006.

title: Implement the pending-invitations read endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An Owner/Admin can list a workspace's pending invitations through a PII-safe projection (invited email is the only personal datum and the token hash is never returned); results are tenant/workspace-scoped; non-privileged roles and foreign tenants are denied.
required_tests: Integration: Owner/Admin lists pending invites; a non-privileged role is 403; a foreign tenant is hidden-404; the response never contains the token hash (T6/T7).
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (manage-members has no way to see outstanding invites). Add GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations returning pending invitations (id, invited email, role, status, expiry) and never the token hash. Reuse WorkspaceInvitationRepository (add a ListPendingByWorkspace query if absent) and the existing WorkspaceEndpoints Owner/Admin authorization. Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08. Pairs with CORE-WS-006/007.

title: Implement the scene reorder endpoint
acceptance_criteria: A host can move a scene to a new position within its workspace; the workspace scene ordering re-packs deterministically with no gaps or duplicates; reordering is authorized and tenant/workspace-scoped; concurrent reorders do not corrupt the order.
required_tests: Integration: reordering a scene yields the expected (scene_order, id) sequence; an out-of-range or foreign scene is hidden-404; a non-authoring role is 403; two concurrent reorders converge without duplicate orders (with CORE-CONC-006).
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (scenes can only be appended-to-end and re-packed on delete; there is no explicit user-driven reorder). Program.cs ~354-355 names the reorder route as a later story and csv/api_routes.csv has no reorder route (only GET list, POST create, DELETE, GET by-id). Add e.g. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/scenes/{sceneId}/reorder (or a PUT with a target index). Reuse the CORE-SCENE-001 (scene_order, id) ordering and the delete-repack logic; assign order server-side (no client-trusted absolute order). Authorize Host/CoHost/Owner/Admin exactly like scene create (SceneEndpoints.cs ~360-366). Benefits from CORE-CONC-006 (Scene.Reorder is a real read-modify-write). Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08.

title: Emit or formally prune the unemitted session events
acceptance_criteria: Every event in csv/event_catalog.csv is either actually emitted by a Core command or explicitly removed from the catalog (or marked deferred with a named owner), so the catalog is a contract not aspirational; the spec-consistency check validates the emitted set against the non-deferred catalog.
required_tests: Integration: each newly-emitted event (SessionCreated on session create, SceneCreated on scene create, ContentBlockCreated on content-block create, RecapGenerated on recap generation) persists and reaches its documented recipients with identifier-only payloads (no PII, T7); a spec-consistency test fails if the catalog lists a non-deferred event that no command emits.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (spec-integrity; the session-event analogue of CORE-SPEC-002, which made the entitlement/store catalog real). docs/24 'Genuinely deferred items' records that 7 catalog events are documented but unemitted: the emitted set is the 8 names in apps/api/Realtime/SessionEventTypes.cs (SessionStarted/Ended, ParticipantJoined/Left, SceneActivated, VisibilityRuleChanged, ContentRevealed/Hidden) while csv/event_catalog.csv and docs/09 list 15. DECIDED (2026-06-15): EMIT the 4 that tie to an existing Core command - SessionCreated on POST .../sessions, SceneCreated on scene create, ContentBlockCreated on content-block create, RecapGenerated on the recap worker job - via the existing ISessionEventPublisher + SessionEventRecipientResolver, payload identifier-only (T7), inside the CORE-CONC-002 transaction; PRUNE the 3 vertical/future ones - PrivateMessageSent, AssetRevealed, SessionNoteCreated - by removing them from csv/event_catalog.csv and docs/09 and recording them as deferred-to-vertical in docs/24. Then extend scripts/spec-consistency.ps1 to check the emitted set vs the non-deferred catalog (CORE-SPEC-001 checks docs/09 vs csv only, never emission). Reuse SessionEventTypes + the publisher; never widen an audience (subject-gated events stay gated).

title: Record the deliberately-absent capabilities and authorization model as explicit decisions
acceptance_criteria: Each capability that exists in the model but is deliberately not exposed (export/recap read endpoints, entity / entity-type / template create and list endpoints, preview-as-participant), each known spec contradiction, and the deliberate inline-authorization decision are recorded as explicit dated deferrals/decisions naming the owner (Core-later vs vertical) and rationale, so a reader can tell an intentional omission from a gap.
required_tests: Doc/CSV consistency stays green (the CORE-SPEC-001 checks); no Core source change.
notes: TIER 4 LOW (hygiene; docs/csv only, no new endpoints). Consolidate the many are later stories and are deliberately not built/wired here markers into one explicit deferral/decision register (extend docs/24 'Genuinely deferred items' or add a docs section), mirroring how CORE-DOC-002 and CORE-DR-004 formalized deferrals: (a) the deliberately-absent read/CRUD endpoints - Program.cs ~358/401/423/445/482/500/710/1304, ExportManifestProjection.cs ~146 and ExportJob.cs ~239 (no export read/download route), Recap.cs ~32-55 (no recap read route), the Entity/EntityType/Template/Visibility explicit-ids contract notes, ContentBlockEndpoints.cs ~41; CORE-E2E-003 already records recap/export have no HTTP read endpoints by design. (b) Reconcile the active-scene contradiction: Program.cs ~354 says a session activates a scene through its active scene pointer in a later story, but SessionEventTypes.cs ~63 states revealing a scene IS the scene switch (no separate active-scene command) - decide whether an explicit active-scene pointer is a real future feature or reveal-is-activation is the final contract, and record the decision. (c) Note the session-participant roster deferral (docs/11 ~55; SessionEventRecipientResolver.cs ~54) is a deliberate design (correctness held by session-keyed groups + the session-scoped gate), not a gap. (d) Record that per-action authorization is INLINE by deliberate decision: CORE-WS-005 chose no policy framework because the inline endpoint checks carry security-relevant ORDERING (404-before-403, membership-before-role, existence-before-state) that a capability-policy extraction would risk collapsing - a consolidated authorization policy is explicitly NOT pursued and is not a gap. This only makes the deferrals/decisions auditable; it adds no endpoints. Pairs with CORE-SPEC-001/CORE-EVT-004.
